source_extracts.label: FedEx — What is Dimensional Weight? (billable weight rule)
source_extracts.quote: For each shipment, you are charged based on the dimensional weight or actual weight of the package—whichever is greater.

source_extracts.label: FedEx — What is Dimensional Weight? (139 divisor)
source_extracts.quote: Dividing by 139 for U.S., Puerto Rico, and international shipments.

source_extracts.label: UPS — Shipping Package Dimensions and Weight (dim weight formula + divisors)
source_extracts.quote: To calculate dimensional weight: Dimensional Weight = (L x W x H) ÷ Divisor ... Note: The divisor varies by rate type: 139 for Daily Rates; 166 for Retail Rates.

source_extracts.label: UPS — Shipping Package Dimensions and Weight (size/weight limits)
source_extracts.quote: UPS packages can weight up to a maximum 150 lbs. The maximum length for UPS packages is 108 inches. ... Packages can be up to 165 inches in length and girth combined.

source_extracts.label: USPS — Ground Advantage (delivery window, weight cap, starting price)
source_extracts.quote: USPS Ground Advantage® service is an affordable and reliable way to send packages inside the U.S. ... Prices start at $8.40 at a Post Office™ location. ... For mailable items up to 70 lbs. Expected delivery in 2–5 days.

source_extracts.label: USPS — Priority Mail (delivery window, flat rate, starting price)
source_extracts.quote: Priority Mail® service includes tracking and delivery in 2-3 days. ... Priority Mail Flat Rate® products let you ship packages up to 70 lbs to any state at the same price. ... Prices start at $11.50 at a Post Office.

source_extracts.label: Mailbox Plus Source of Truth — all-four-carrier authorization, live-rate pull phrasing, packing capabilities, approved visit-speed phrasing
source_extracts.quote: All four major carriers: Authorized shipping center and drop-off outlet for USPS, UPS, FedEx, and DHL; 'We pull live rates from all four carriers — UPS, FedEx, USPS, and DHL — side by side'; 'most visits are done in under ten minutes' is approved.

scope_rules: Every carrier figure is attributed to that carrier's own official page, fetched live on 2026-11-21; no figure is sourced from model memory or from the legacy article.

The legacy article's invented prices ($18.47/$17.92/$15.80/$14.50), invented competitor locations (UPS Store 'Mentor Avenue', FedEx Office 'SOM Center Road', 'no DHL retail store within ten miles'), invented drive/wait times, 'under three minutes' / 'two minutes and forty seconds' turnaround promises, and invented cost math ('seventy hours a year', 'forty to eighty dollars a month', 'five hundred to a thousand dollars a year') are all REMOVED — none reappear in any form.
DHL is described only via the owner-approved all-four-carriers store claim; no characterization of DHL's U.S. retail role is made (unverifiable at fetch time, so cut).
Rate-chart criticism stays hedged/qualitative ('typically', 'often', 'can'); no invented dollar spreads or time-loss figures.
USPS starting prices are labeled as starting points 'at a Post Office' with online/commercial rates lower, exactly as USPS frames them.
required_when: Any edit adding a rate figure, divisor, weight/size limit, delivery window, price, address, phone number, or time promise to this article must register it here first and add a receipt row.
